title: Sync pull fills its page limit across all tables, instead of limit/N rows per table with the cursor held at the earliest full table (257 calls per rep snapshot down to about ceil(R/500)+1)
rootCause:
One server defect in SyncService.pull causes both symptoms. The client needs no change.

1. Budget per table. sync.service.ts:278 sets `perTable = floor(limit / tables.length)` and :293 passes it to every handler. A salesperson holds 21 tables (sync-tables.ts:73-117, the SALES and EVERY_DEVICE rows). The engine asks for 500 (engine.ts:52, :434), so each table gets 23 rows. tablePull reads 24 and takes the 23rd row's instant as its watermark (sync.registry.ts:292-301).

2. The cursor waits for the slowest table. sync.service.ts:297-300 and :311-312 move the cursor only to the EARLIEST watermark among the full tables. Each call therefore advances by 23 rows of whichever table is densest at the cursor, and every table that was not full re-sends everything it holds after the cursor on the next call. In api-02-order-page-network.txt, each call returns changes for 11-19 tables.

3. Evidence, re-checked.
   - The finding's decoded cursors `.655701Z`, `.656751Z` and `.657478Z` are exactly rows 23, 46 and 69 of the pilot tenant's `price_list_items`, ordered by (updated_at, id) in dos_qa. That table has 696 rows and 696 distinct instants, so there are no ties.
   - ~/.dos-qa-logs/logs/sales-service.log now holds 6,756 GET /sync/pull calls in 26 runs (a run starts at a call without `since`): 25 runs of 257-262 calls on devices 01a0973d… and 01a09785…, and one run of 277 on 01a0975f…, between 2026-09-13 01:39 and 03:55.

4. The finding's mechanism is wrong. Rows do NOT share a timestamp: `dos_touch_updated_at` stamps `clock_timestamp()` per row (migrations/0040_sync_delta_guarantees.sql:76). Tie completion (sync.registry.ts:302-322) plays no part. A per-table (updated_at, id) keyset cursor is not needed, and it would strain the 256-character `since` cap (contracts/src/sync.ts:227).

5. "~55 per screen open" is a WEB PAGE RELOAD restarting the snapshot, not a mount bug.
   - `expo start --web` is not cross-origin isolated (no COOP/COEP header anywhere in frontend/), so openStore falls back to the memory store (libs/offline/src/store/open.web.ts:19-29, :41-50) and the cursor dies with the page.
   - In api-02-order-page-network.txt line 5, the first pull after the reload carries no `since`. QA/tools/pw.mjs `goto` (:21) is a full page load.
   - In-app navigation does not restart the engine:
     - OfflineProvider sits above the gate (sales-app/app/_layout.tsx:169-257).
     - Its effect deps are [enabled, deviceId, storeFactory, databaseName, pullIntervalMs, tenantId] (offline/src/react.tsx:112).
     - The sales wrapper passes the module-level `openStore` and a memoised device id (_layout.tsx:281-302).
     - The session stays non-null while hydrating.
   - pullLoop echoes the cursor correctly (engine.ts:414-445).

6. The 401 on /sync/manifest and the 220 /auth/refresh calls belong to DOS-089 (P3), not this finding.

7. A latent defect on the same lines goes away with the rewrite rather than being fixed separately.
   - sync.service.ts:311 compares a microsecond watermark with `sinceText` as strings.
   - A cursor issued from `asOf` has only millisecond precision (`toISOString`).
   - So a watermark inside that same millisecond sorts before it ('…00.123456Z' < '…00.123Z'). The cursor stands still and the device repeats the page until the engine's 1000-page guard throws.

changes.what:
`pull()` (:261-315):
- Delete `perTable` (:278). Call every handler with `limit: input.limit` and `untilText: until` (starts null).
- Keep `wm`/`mark` for tables whose result has `hasMore` (:282-289, :297-300). Set `saturated = true` when any table has it.
- Collect `pages: {table, result}[]` and `held`: the NON-EMPTY instants of `result.at` and `result.deletedAt`.
- After each handler, when `held.length > limit` (strict): set `overflow = true`, sort `held`, keep its first `limit` entries, and set `until = held[limit-1]`. Later tables then read no further than that instant. Using `>=` would skip rows (DOS-080 test 3).
- After the loop:
  - `hasMore = saturated || overflow`
  - `pinned = saturated && wm.at === ''` (a table could not finish a tie of more than 2000 rows)
  - if `hasMore && !pinned`: `cut = earliest(held.sort()[limit-1] when held.length >= limit, wm.at when not null)`. Without `wm.at`, a tombstone page thinned by the still-visible filter lets the cut pass that table's unread tombstones (DOS-080 test 4).
- Build `changes` from `pages`:
  - When `cut` is set, keep only rows and deleted ids whose instant is <= cut. An empty instant is kept.
  - Otherwise (a complete pass, or the pinned case) keep everything.
  - Keep the rule `rows.length>0 || deleted.length>0 || since===null`.
- `cursor = !hasMore ? encodeCursor(asOf) : encodeCursor(cut ?? sinceText ?? EPOCH)`. The pinned case keeps today's behaviour exactly.
- Do NOT port the string compare `wm.at > sinceText` (:311). Every instant in `held` and every watermark comes from SQL bounded by `> since`, so `cut` is later than `since` by construction. That compare is also wrong when `sinceText` came from `asOf` at millisecond precision (root cause 7).
- Rewrite the doc comments at :261-268, :294-296 and :304-309: a page is the `limit` earliest changes (rows and tombstones, by instant) across the read set, ties completed, and the cursor is the last instant the page delivered.

- `PullRequest` (:23-36): add `untilText: string | null`, meaning rows and tombstones at or before this instant only, in the same microsecond ISO form as `sinceText`.
- `PullResult` (:38-60):
  - Add required `at: string[]` (instant of each row, same order as `rows`) and `deletedAt: string[]` (instant of each id in `deleted`).
  - `hasMore` is unchanged.
  - Rewrite the `watermark` comment (:53-59): the service cuts the page at the earlier of the page budget's last instant and the earliest watermark among the full tables.
- `tablePull` handler (:284-341):
  - Add `${request.untilText ? sql`and updated_at <= ${request.untilText}::timestamptz` : sql``}` to `where` (:287-289), so it also bounds the tie query.
  - Build `at = raw.map(r => instantOf(r) ?? '')` before `__sync_at` is stripped (:324-329).
  - Return `at` and `deletedAt`.
- `readTombstones` (:441-492):
  - When `untilText` is set, add `and t.deleted_at <= ${untilText}::timestamptz` to the first query (:455-460). The tie query (:470-476) is already bounded by its watermark, which is <= until.
  - After the still-in-scope filter (:480-491), keep ids and instants paired: `kept = rows.filter(r => !survivors.has(r.row_id))`, returning `{ ids: kept.map(r => r.row_id), at: kept.map(r => r.__sync_at), hasMore, watermark }`.
  - Both early returns (:452, :462) give `at: []`.
- Tie completion, TIE_COMPLETION_LIMIT, the watermark and combineWatermarks are unchanged.
- All 37 registrations go through tablePull (the billing, catalog, delivery, inventory, orders, pricing, receivables, retailers, tenant-catalog and warehouse modules), so no other handler needs the new fields.

Line 32: the `desk_only` stub returns `{ rows: [{ id: 'x' }], at: [''], deleted: [], deletedAt: [] }` to satisfy the new required PullResult fields. An empty instant stays out of the page budget and is always kept.

No assertion changes. The pulls in this file hold only `beats` for a fresh tenant plus the stub, and no global catalog table is registered, so one page still carries everything.

WHY EXISTING TESTS MUST MOVE
After the fix, page 1 is the `limit` EARLIEST changes. The four global catalog tables (catalog.module.ts:30-33, no tenant predicate) hold rows older than this describe's fixtures: 288 from the seed in dos_qa, plus the rows 16 spec files add to the test database on every run. A default-limit (200) page 1 is therefore catalog rows only.
- Four tests would FAIL on page 1:
  - 'gives a shop only the rows linked to its own shop…' (`links.length > 0`, `items.length` 2)
  - 'sends every value in the shape its own manifest declared…' (`bill.rows[0].total_paise`)
  - 'gives the shop its own bill and the desk both shops…' (`toEqual([shopId])`)
  - 'sends a delta after a change, and a tombstone after a delete' (mid-pass cursors)
- Two would silently check less: the rows half of 'never sends a cost, margin or landed-cost column to a %s device', and 'does not report a row that merely moved to another reader…'.

HELPERS (added once, next to `pullOf`)
- `pagesOf(actor, query)`: loops `pullOf` while hasMore, echoing the last cursor, with a guard of 200 pages (throws past it). Returns the page bodies.
- `drainOf(actor, query)`:
  - Runs `pagesOf` with `limit: '500'` unless the query names one.
  - Merges per table: rows keyed by that table's `primaryKey` from `manifestOf(actor)`, a later copy replacing an earlier one as the device's upsert does; `deleted` as a set in arrival order.
  - Returns `{ status, body: { changes, cursor: <last cursor>, hasMore: false, asOf: <last asOf> } }`.
- `markCursor()`:
  - Reads `select to_char(clock_timestamp() at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as t` through `db`.
  - Returns base64url `{v:1,t}`, the format documented at sync.service.ts:363-372.
  - Used by tests 2-4 so a delta starts exactly after the fixture, with no 5 s overlap.

REFACTOR: same assertions, evaluated on the pass (docs/07 rule 3) instead of page 1
- Switch these six tests from `pullOf` to `drainOf`:
  - the shop/tier test (shopPull, deskPull)
  - the value-shape test (pull)
  - the cost-column test (the snapshot in its rows half)
  - the shop/desk/rep bill test (shopPull, repPull, deskPull)
  - the delta/tombstone test (first, delta, before, after, gone; `first` keeps `limit: '500'`)
  - the moved-row test (before, desk)
- Leave these untouched:
  - 'registers a pull for all 37 tables…'
  - 'serves %s exactly the tables…' and 'pulls the global catalog…' (a page-1 table list, which still holds through the `since === null` rule)
  - the shop write-queue test
  - 'advances the cursor when a page is full…'
  - the LWW veto test and the upload replay test

NEW
Append the four DOS-080 tests LAST in the describe, after 'replays an upload batch twice…', so their beats and locations cannot affect earlier tests. Fixtures and assertions are in `verify`.

- Line 22: replace "`limit` is shared across the tables in the call; `hasMore` means at least one table filled its share" with: `limit` is the page size across the whole read set; a page holds the `limit` earliest changes (rows and tombstones, by instant, ties completed); `hasMore` means something lies past the page.
- Line 22 (same paragraph) and line 34: replace "to the earliest point every table has finished" with "to the last instant the page delivered".
- The cursor format `{v:1,t}` and the 5 s overlap are unchanged.

contractChange:
none.
- SyncPullInput and SyncPullOutput (contracts/src/sync.ts:225-240) are unchanged.
- `limit` is already documented as "Rows per call across all tables" (:229), which is exactly the behaviour after the fix.
- The cursor stays base64url `{v:1,t:<µs instant>}`. Devices mid-snapshot at deploy continue, and mixed-version instances in a rolling deploy stay compatible: each side reads `> since` from a row instant.
- PullRequest and PullResult are internal to @dos/core (sync.registry.ts, re-exported as types from the sync index only), and all 37 registrations go through tablePull.
- No README regeneration is needed.
migration: none. The (tenant_id, updated_at) indexes, the clock_timestamp() touch trigger, the tombstone triggers and sync_tombstones_table_idx (tenant_id, table_name, deleted_at) already exist (migrations 0038-0040). The new `<= until` bound is a range on the same indexes.

tests.name: DOS-080 fills the page limit across tables: a snapshot of a 60-beat burst takes at most ceil((rows+tombstones)/limit)+1 calls and delivers every row exactly once
DOS-080 a delta whose updates and tombstones overflow the page delivers each of them exactly once across the pages
DOS-080 a first table that fills the page exactly does not hide a later table's changes
DOS-080 a tombstone page thinned by the still-visible filter does not let the cursor pass that table's unread tombstones

verify:
SPECS
1. On the unfixed tree, write the helpers, the six drainOf refactors and the four DOS-080 tests, then run `cd backend && pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/sync -t DOS-080`. All four DOS-080 tests must fail:
   - test 1 needs 20+ pages and re-sends locations;
   - tests 2-4 re-send rows.
   Do not use the six refactored tests as fail-first evidence. On the unfixed tree a full drain of the global catalog on a polluted `dos` database can hit the 30 s test timeout (libs/config/vitest.preset.js:8), which is the storm itself.
2. Apply the fix and run `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/sync`. Expect the four DOS-080 tests and every existing test in sync.spec.ts and sync.coverage.spec.ts to pass, including the six on `drainOf` and 'advances the cursor when a page is full…'.

TEST 1 (snapshot burst, owner)
- Insert 60 beats for `tenantId`, one INSERT each, so every row gets its own clock_timestamp. Wait 20 ms, then insert 12 locations (kind 'warehouse').
- Count through `db`:
  - R = the tenant's beats + locations + stock_lots;
  - T = `sync_tombstones` rows for the tenant in those three tables. At least one exists: the `locations` row deleted by the earlier delta test, which a later page (carrying `since`) may deliver.
- Run `pagesOf(owner, { 'tables[0]': 'beats', 'tables[1]': 'locations', 'tables[2]': 'stock_lots', limit: '10' })`.
- Assert:
  - pages <= ceil((R+T)/10)+1;
  - every page with hasMore carries at least 10 rows+deleted;
  - every tenant id of the three tables appears exactly once in rows across the pass;
  - no id appears twice in deleted.
- The third table is read after locations has already overflowed the page, so the `untilText` path runs.

TEST 2 (interleaved updates and tombstones, owner)
- Insert 30 beats one by one, then take `since = markCursor()`.
- For i in 0..14: delete beat[2i], then rename beat[2i+1].
- Run `pagesOf(owner, { 'tables[0]': 'beats', limit: '10', since })`.
- Assert:
  - deleted, across the pass, is exactly the 15 deleted ids, each once;
  - beats rows are exactly the 15 renamed ids, each once, carrying the new names;
  - no id is in both.
- Before the fix, the rows page and the tombstone page stop at different instants, and the half that ran further is re-sent.

TEST 3 (strict `>`, owner)
- Insert 10 locations, then take `since = markCursor()`.
- Rename those 10. Wait 20 ms, then insert 5 beats.
- Run `pagesOf(owner, { 'tables[0]': 'locations', 'tables[1]': 'beats', limit: '10', since })`.
- Assert: rows are exactly the 10 location ids once each and the 5 beat ids once each; the last page has hasMore false.
- Locations fill the page exactly without being full (the handler reads 11 and gets 10). An implementation that sets `until` at `held.length >= limit` reads beats `<=` the 10th location instant, gets none, answers hasMore false and ends the pass without the beats.
- Before the fix: perTable = 5, so beats are re-sent.

TEST 4 (full-table watermark guard, owner)
- Insert 11 locations L1..L11, then take `since = markCursor()`.
- Delete L1..L10 one statement each, then delete L11. Wait 20 ms, then re-insert L1..L10 with the same ids and names. Their tombstones stay, because `dos_record_tombstone` upserts (0040:81-91) and nothing clears a tombstone on insert.
- Run `pagesOf(owner, { 'tables[0]': 'locations', limit: '10', since })`.
- Assert:
  - L11 appears in deleted exactly once;
  - L1..L10 appear in rows exactly once each and never in deleted.
- Correct paging:
  - Page 1: the tombstone read is full (11 > 10), but all ten ids it keeps are alive and filtered out. The rows (instants r1..r10) are all later than L11's tombstone t11. Cut = the tombstone watermark t10, so the page is empty with hasMore true.
  - Page 2: L1..L9 and L11.
  - Page 3: L10.
- A cut without `wm.at` lands at r10, and t11 is never read again: L11 stays on the device for ever.
- Before the fix: L1..L10 are re-sent on page 2.

risk:
1. Skipping a row is the one unrecoverable failure.
   - Why the cut cannot skip: every table is complete up to min(budget-th instant, earliest full-table watermark).
     - A table that filled its rows page put `limit` instants at or before its watermark into `held`, so the budget-th instant is no later than that watermark.
     - A table that filled only its tombstone page is covered by `wm.at`, even when the still-visible filter removed its ids from `held` (test 4).
     - A table read with `until` is complete to `until`. `until` only ever moves earlier, and the final budget-th instant is never later than it.
   - Rows at the cut instant are complete: a table that ran past the cut includes them, and a table that stopped exactly at the cut completed the tie.
   - `held` must use strict `>` (test 3) and non-empty instants only; an empty instant would give an empty cut and the next call would get a 400 on the cursor.

2. Six existing coverage tests change from reading page 1 to reading the pass through `drainOf`.
   - The assertions are identical; only the unit changes, to what a device holds after rule 3 of docs/07.
   - This is not a weakening. Left on page 1, four would fail, and the cost-column rows check would quietly cover only catalog rows.
   - Cost: a full drain reads the global catalog at 500 per call. Watch the 30 s test timeout on a heavily polluted `dos` database. The first fallback is to name `tables` on the delta test's two full drains (`first`, `before`), which only assert on locations and stock_balances.

3. Per-call database and memory work rises while total work falls.
   - The first two handlers read up to limit+1 rows (+ ties) before `until` exists. Later tables read up to limit+1 rows each at or before `until`.
   - Worst case before trimming: about 21×501 rows for a rep and 37×501 for the desk, against 21×24 today. Calls fall about 20×, and the response stays within docs/20 rule 3 (500).

4. Pinned edge: more than 2000 rows in one microsecond of one table (TIE_COMPLETION_LIMIT) behaves exactly as today. The cursor stays and the page is not trimmed. Not in scope.

5. Web memory store: a reload still re-snapshots, by design (docs/27 §2). It is now cheap, but not zero.

6. Overlap, unchanged:
   - The last page of a pass still sets cursor = asOf - 5 s.
   - Mid-pass cursors carry no overlap, today or after the fix. A transaction that stamps a row before a mid-pass cut and commits after that read is missed in both versions. Not in scope.

7. Held DOS-032+059 changes the receipts manifest (series_code, fy), so delivery and retailer devices re-snapshot once after it. With this fix that takes a handful of calls, not hundreds. There is no file overlap and no ordering dependency.
reviewNotes:
WHAT I CHANGED

1. Existing tests.
   - The plan said every existing sync test passes after the fix. Four in sync.coverage.spec.ts would fail and two would quietly check less.
   - The cause: the fix makes page 1 the `limit` earliest changes, and the four global catalog tables (no tenant predicate, catalog.module.ts:30-33) hold rows older than the describe's fixtures. That is 288 from the seed alone in dos_qa, above the default limit of 200.
   - Added the `pagesOf`/`drainOf` helpers and moved those six named tests onto the pass with identical assertions. `drainOf` dedups by the manifest primaryKey, as the device upsert does, so the refactored tests stay about content, not paging.

2. Test 1's page bound now includes tombstones. The earlier delta test deletes a `locations` row in the same tenant, and snapshot pages after the first carry `since`, so that tombstone can be delivered. The plan's ceil(R/10)+1 could have been off by one.

3. Tests 2-4 take their `since` from `markCursor()` (the database clock, µs, the documented cursor format) instead of a drained cursor, so they assert exact sets, free of the 5 s overlap. Test 2 now names `tables[0]=beats`.

4. Added tests 3 and 4. The plan's reviewNotes (a) strict `>` and (b) the `wm.at` term are exactly the two mistakes that silently skip rows, and neither of the plan's two tests could catch them. I hand-simulated both tests on the unfixed code, the correct fix, and the wrong variants.

5. Verify step 5 was not executable as written. Sign-out does not wipe the store (`SyncEngine.wipe()`, engine.ts:187, has no caller), so the plan's sign-out/sign-in would have produced a delta, not a snapshot. It now uses `pm clear in.distributionos.sales`, as QA/tools/android-login.sh:20 does.

6. Changes additions:
   - the registry's `watermark` doc comment (:53-59);
   - an explicit instruction not to port the `wm.at > sinceText` string compare (:311), a latent stall when `sinceText` came from a millisecond `asOf`;
   - the `desk_only` stub uses `at: ['']` rather than a 1970 instant.

7. Evidence corrections:
   - 26 runs of 257-277 calls, not all exactly 257; 6,756 GET pulls in the current log.
   - The finding's third cursor is row 69, which confirms the 23-row stride.
   - 11,968 re-counted in dos_qa; it includes the 288 global rows.
   - The pilot tenant has 2 tombstones, so the ≤ 25 bound holds.

8. Platforms: added ios. The server fix reaches every device; its verification is optional.

CONFIRMED BY READING
- Every cited line.
- All 37 pull registrations use tablePull.
- No spec outside modules/sync calls /sync/pull.
- sync_tombstones is keyed (tenant_id, table_name, row_id) with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (0040:88-90).
- The provider effect deps and the stable storeFactory in the sales wrapper.
- There is no COOP/COEP header in frontend/.
- None of the held plans (DOS-032+059, 074+097, 096, 003, 004, 106, 043, 007, 056) or the batch-2 plans touches sync.service.ts, sync.registry.ts, sync.spec.ts, sync.coverage.spec.ts or docs/07. DOS-115 changes upload handlers in orders.sync.ts only.

COULD NOT CONFIRM
- I could not query the `dos` test database (read access was dos_qa only), so the number of global catalog rows older than the coverage fixtures there is inferred: a seeded database plus 16 spec files that add global rows per run. On a fresh CI database with no seed, the page-1 tests might still pass after the fix. On the founder's database they would not.
- Ran no test; the paging was simulated by hand.
- iOS not exercised.

RESIDUAL DOUBTS
- Peak memory per request rises (risk 3). A two-phase read (instants first, then rows at or before the cut) would bound it at the price of double queries. Not proposed.
- The global catalog is not narrowed per tenant (catalog.module.ts:30-33): every device snapshots the whole curated master, and at production scale that will dominate a first sync. This is a separate finding, not this fix.
- The comment at engine.ts:422-426 ("265 for a salesperson") goes stale. Left untouched so the client stays unchanged.
- docs/27 §5 item 2 ("Snapshots carry no tombstones") is true only of the first page. Pre-existing, not changed.

CHECK SPECIFICALLY
(a) Strict `held.length > limit` for `until`.
(b) `cut` = the earlier of the budget-th instant and `wm.at`.
(c) readTombstones keeps ids and instants paired after the survivors filter, and applies `until` to its first query.
(d) tablePull takes `at` from `raw` (after tie completion) before `__sync_at` is stripped.
(e) The pinned path does not trim.
(f) The sync.spec.ts stub change is type-only.
(g) The service comments, the registry watermark comment and docs/07 lines 22 and 34 describe the new page semantics.
(h) No client change; engine.ts and its tests are untouched.
(i) The four DOS-080 tests come LAST in the describe.
(j) The six drainOf refactors change no assertion.
(k) The `wm.at > sinceText` compare is not carried over.

THE SUGGESTED FIX, CORRECTED
- The server half is right in intent (fill `limit`) but wrong in mechanism. Rows do not share timestamps, and the one-instant cursor is sound. The defect is the limit/N budget plus a cursor that waits for the earliest full table.
- A per-table keyset cursor would need a contract change (`since` is capped at 256 characters) and is not required.
- The client half needs no change. Re-pulls happen on web page reloads onto the memory store (docs/27 §2); QA's pw.mjs `goto` is a full reload. They do not happen on screen mounts.

- Serving COOP/COEP from the dev Metro would let QA web walks use OPFS the way the hosted site does (open.web.ts comment, docs/26).
